title: Carney Chukwuemeka receives first Austria call up after switching allegiance from England
content:
Carney Chukwuemeka has received his first call-up to the Austrian international squad after switching allegiance from England.

Borussia Dortmund’s Chukwuemeka, formerly an England youth international who played for Chelsea and Aston Villa in the Premier League, was born in Austria and had his change of registration approved by FIFA last week.

Ralf Rangnick has named the 22-year-old midfielder in the squad for the upcoming friendlies against Ghana on March 27 and South Korea three days later. Rangnick’s Austria have already qualified for the World Cup, where they will face Jordan, Algeria and Argentina in Group J.

For Rangnick, this is the culmination of a two-year pursuit. Chukwuemeka was first approached about playing for Austria in 2024, before that year’s European Championship. Rangnick had seen influential midfielder Xaver Schlager suffer a serious injury playing for RB Leipzig, and was interested in both a replacement for the tournament and a player who could be impactful in a different way.

Ultimately, Chukwuemeka was not ready; in addition to being qualified for England, he was eligible to play for Nigeria through his parents, too, and was not ready to commit his international future.

That changed in late 2025, when Chukwuemeka and Rangnick spoke again, with the player by then having changed his mind.

The change arrives at an interesting moment in his career. Chukwuemeka moved to Dortmund from Chelsea in January 2025. Initially he joined on loan, before signing permanently in the summer. He has been impactful and influential, but only sparingly, and has struggled for fitness and continuity. He has only started seven games for Dortmund across all competitions this season, playing fewer than 1000 minutes combined.

But Rangnick is confident that he’s a match for his direct, physical style of football, and sees Chukwuemeka as a rare and offensively destructive player, who can potentially become a real asset to an Austrian side that does not currently possess someone of similar profile.

Chukwuemeka is not the only new addition to Rangnick’s squad.

Paul Wanner, 20, a former Bayern Munich midfielder who joined PSV Eindhoven last summer, has received his first call up, too, having also only just declared for Austria.

For a long time, Wanner was a great hope at Bayern, whose academy he joined as a 13-year-old. He was seen briefly as having the talent to potentially become a starter at Allianz Arena, with ability on the scale of someone like Florian Wirtz or Jamal Musiala. He was extremely well thought of by the German Football Association (DFB), too, and despite being born in Austria, he represented Germany at all age groups, from U17 upwards.

The question of his international future has been a topic for many months, with Wanner wrestling with the decision for several years. For Rangnick, this has been an even longer pursuit; the first conversation between him and Wanner happened in October 2022, a few months after the former Manchester United interim head coach was appointed.

And in March 2025, Wanner announced that he was ready to commit to Austria, telling Sky Sports: “This decision was probably the hardest of my career. Because of my parents, my upbringing, and the various stages of my career, I have two hearts beating in my chest.

“I am incredibly honored that two federations tried to convince me to play for their national teams. I’ve been in constant communication with the Austrian Football Association (ÖFB), and I’ve had a very open and honest exchange with Ralf Rangnick and his coaching staff for a long time. We’ve intensified this even further in recent weeks.”

He is also now in position to make his debut against Ghana in Vienna.

There are no guarantees that either player will make the World Cup squad. Austria are well-stocked in midfield, with Christoph Baumgartner, Marcel Sabitzer, Romano Schmid and the fit-again Schlager all, among others, competing for starting positions, but both will have an opportunity to be selected for what will be their new nation’s first World Cup appearance since 1998.
